content.text: {"primary_meaning":"Light most commonly symbolizes God’s holy and life-giving presence as revealed truth and goodness: it discloses reality, guides people, brings salvation and life, and stands opposed to the darkness of sin, evil, ignorance, and death.","primary_basis":["Psalm 27:1 — the Lord is described as the psalmist’s light and salvation.","Psalm 36:9 — in God’s light people see light, linking light with divine life and revelation.","Psalm 119:105,130 — God’s word is a lamp and gives light, symbolizing guidance and understanding.","Isaiah 9:2 — light dawns upon people walking in darkness, commonly interpreted in terms of deliverance and messianic salvation.","Isaiah 60:1-3,19-20 — God’s glory and everlasting presence are portrayed as Israel’s light.","John 1:4-9 — the divine Word is the true light that gives life and enlightens humanity.","John 8:12 — Jesus identifies himself as the light of the world, giving the light of life.","2 Corinthians 4:6 — light symbolizes the knowledge of God’s glory revealed in Christ.","1 John 1:5-7 — “God is light,” with light associated with divine holiness, truth, and faithful fellowship.","Revelation 21:23-25; 22:5 — God and the Lamb illuminate the renewed creation, where darkness is absent."],"alternatives":[{"meaning":"Light specifically symbolizes Jesus Christ as the Messiah and revealer of God, rather than divine presence or truth in a broader sense.","basis":["Isaiah 9:2","John 1:4-9","John 8:12","John 9:5","John 12:35-36,46","Luke 2:30-32"],"prominence":"dominant"},{"meaning":"Light symbolizes the faithful witness and righteous conduct of God’s people, who reflect divine truth before the world.","basis":["Isaiah 42:6; 49:6","Matthew 5:14-16","Luke 11:33-36","Acts 13:47","Philippians 2:15","Ephesians 5:8-14"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Light symbolizes moral purity and righteousness, especially conduct that contrasts with sinful “works of darkness.”","basis":["John 3:19-21","Romans 13:12-13","Ephesians 5:8-14","1 Thessalonians 5:5-8","1 John 1:5-7; 2:8-11"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Light symbolizes knowledge, understanding, or revelation, particularly illumination given through God’s word or gospel.","basis":["Psalm 119:105,130","Daniel 2:22","2 Corinthians 4:4-6","Ephesians 1:17-18","2 Peter 1:19"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Light symbolizes salvation, hope, flourishing, and renewed life after oppression, suffering, or death.","basis":["Job 33:28,30","Psalm 27:1","Isaiah 9:2","Isaiah 58:8-10","Micah 7:8-9","Matthew 4:16"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Light functions as exposure and judgment: it reveals hidden deeds and makes moral reality manifest, not merely comforting or saving.","basis":["John 3:19-21","1 Corinthians 4:5","Ephesians 5:11-13"],"prominence":"minority"},{"meaning":"In some passages light denotes ordinary created light, daylight, life, prosperity, or public visibility without carrying a fixed theological symbol.","basis":["Genesis 1:3-5","Ecclesiastes 11:7","Job 30:26","Matthew 5:15"],"prominence":"common"}],"has_settled_consensus":true,"confidence":"high","notes":"There is a broad and recognizable consensus that light is a positive symbol associated with God, revelation, holiness, life, and salvation in contrast to darkness. Nevertheless, it is polyvalent: context determines whether the immediate referent is God, Christ, Scripture, salvation, moral purity, believers’ witness, or judgment through exposure."}
